description: An employment general counsel must approve the closure package for a workplace-retaliation investigation, including the finding, corrective action, employee placement, governance notification, and insurer coordination, with input from the investigator, human-resources lead, compliance counsel, and insurance specialist.

shared_context.S1: The investigation concerns a manager accused of retaliating against an employee who raised a workplace-conduct complaint.
shared_context.S2: The investigation file is complete and is scheduled for closure at today's legal-team review.
shared_context.S3: The manager currently supervises the complainant, and no corrective-action package has been approved.
shared_context.S4: The firm's closure-review routine requires the investigator, HR, compliance, and insurance functions to report their relevant conclusions before the general counsel approves the package.

PF1.text: Theo completed the final witness-interview comparison this morning and found corroborated evidence that the manager retaliated; under the investigation protocol, the required finding is exactly 'substantiated retaliation,' with a final written warning as the minimum corrective action.

PF2.text: Nadia spoke with the complainant during yesterday's resolution meeting; the complainant agreed to transfer to the Product Compliance team under the Chief Compliance Officer and requested that the manager have no direct supervisory contact for exactly 90 days.

PF3.text: Elias reviewed the audit-committee charter and confirmed that a substantiated retaliation finding involving a director-level manager requires notice to the Audit Committee before the investigation may be closed; the manager is director-level.

PF4.text: Ruth confirmed with the EPL insurer's claims administrator today that this policy requires written insurer notice and written consent before the company approves the closure package for this investigation, including a package containing a substantiated retaliation finding or any monetary resolution.

acceptance_conditions: The finding must be substantiated retaliation, regardless of capitalization.
The corrective action must contain the phrase final written warning.
The complainant must be transferred to the Product Compliance team under the Chief Compliance Officer.
The manager must have no direct supervisory contact with the complainant for exactly 90 days.
Audit Committee notice must be required before closure.
Written insurer notice and consent must be required before approval of the closure package.
The investigator's corroborated finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: 'final written warning' in decisions['corrective_action'] or 'Final written warning' in decisions['corrective_action']
content_checks.C4: 'Chief Compliance Officer' in decisions['new_reporting_line'] or 'Chief Compliance Officer' in decisions['employee_transfer_team']

decisive_facts.why: The shared record does not establish the investigation outcome or discipline; PF1 changes the finding to substantiated retaliation and the corrective action to include a final written warning.
PF2 changes the resolution from an unspecified reporting relationship to transfer to Product Compliance under the Chief Compliance Officer with exactly 90 days of no direct supervision.
PF3 changes the closure package by requiring Audit Committee notice before closure because the finding involves a director-level manager.
PF4 changes the package from ordinary internal closure to requiring written insurer notice and consent before approval of this closure package.
